_comment: Real senate.gov LIS roll-call XML, captured live during story 8.1
(2026-10-19) from the confirmed-working, keyless, public endpoints:
index: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/vote_menu_{congress}_{session}.xml
item:  https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote{congress}{session}/vote_{congress}_{session}_{roll:05d}.xml
Unlike story 5.1's house_rollcalls_sample.json (a hand-built
approximation, because no Congress.gov API key was ever available),
every <roll_call_vote> document below is the BYTE-IDENTICAL root
element this story fetched live, with one trim: each vote's
<members> list (100 senators on a full-attendance vote) is truncated
to the first 5-6 senators AS CAPTURED -- every kept <member> element
is untouched, just fewer of them, to keep this fixture file readable.
Nothing else in any document was edited, reformatted, or invented.
item_nomination / item_cloture_nomination: both roll calls from
vote_menu_119_2's confirmation of Keith Sonderling and Keith Bass --
shows a bare nomination ('On the Nomination', classifies 'other',
since a confirmation is not a vote on legislation) vs. a cloture
vote ON a nomination ('On the Cloture Motion', classifies 'cloture'
regardless of the underlying question being a nomination).
item_amendment: S.Amdt. 5235 to S.Con.Res. 33 -- amendment_number is
populated verbatim ('S.Amdt. 5235'), no reformatting needed unlike
the House source's two-field amendmentType/amendmentNumber pair.
item_cloture_motion_to_proceed: cloture on the motion to proceed to
H.R. 9340 -- the case the module docstring calls out explicitly:
'cloture' must win over 'final_passage' even though the question
names a specific bill, because ending debate is what this vote does.
item_final_passage_118: S. 316 (118th Congress, session 1, vote 77)
-- proves this story's '118th Congress onward' coverage reaches the
actual 118-1 session, not just the 119th, and exercises the clean
'On Passage of the Bill' -> final_passage case.
item_procedural_motion_to_table: H.R. 2670 (118-1, vote 340) -- 'On
the Motion to Table' -> procedural, the Senate's own version of
house_rollcalls's 'previous question'/'motion to table' procedural
class, confirmed from a live sample rather than assumed from memory.
lis_to_bioguide_sample: a small excerpt of the SAME
legislators-current.yaml file app.ingest.legislators already fetches
(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unitedstates/congress-legislators/main/legislators-current.yaml),
confirmed live during this story to carry id.lis beside id.bioguide
on every record -- real {lis_member_id: bioguide} pairs for the
senators who actually appear in the vote documents above (Barrasso
Baldwin S354->B001230, Booker S370->B001288, Blackburn S396->B001243,
Alsobrooks S428->A000382, Banks S429->B001299, Armstrong S440->A000383),
used by tests exercising transform_member_votes_for without a live
network call. 'S999' is deliberately absent from this map -- used by
the unmapped-senator skip scenario (see the feature file).
Used by tests/step_defs/test_senate_rollcalls_steps.py and
tests/test_senate_rollcalls_unit.py. Never fetched over the network
in CI.
